args.description: Filename of the uploaded file.

args.name: metaData
args.description: Optional metadata encoded as a JSON string, such as {"issueId":"..."} or {"commentId":"..."}. These references record upload context; they do not insert the file into that issue or comment. You still need to use assetUrl when creating or updating the content.

args.name: size
args.description: Exact file size in bytes. The upload request must match this size.

fields.name: inboxNotificationUpdate
fields.description: Changes read or snooze state for the authenticated user’s group of related inbox notifications. Supply a notification UUID from the group and at least one state change. The response includes the requested notification and all notifications changed.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the inbox notification to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The inbox state changes to apply.

fields.name: initiativeAddLabel
fields.description: Adds an initiative label while keeping the other labels. Label groups themselves cannot be applied, and the group’s selection rules still apply.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative to add the label to.

args.name: labelId
args.description: The identifier of the label to add.

fields.name: initiativeArchive
fields.description: Archives an initiative.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative to archive.

fields.name: initiativeCreate
fields.description: Creates an initiative in a workspace where initiatives are enabled. You can assign an owner and lead team at creation. Add projects separately with initiativeToProjectCreate, and build a hierarchy with initiativeRelationCreate.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the initiative to create.

fields.name: initiativeDelete
fields.description: Moves an initiative to the trash instead of immediately deleting it permanently. You can restore it with initiativeUnarchive while it remains available.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative to delete.

fields.name: initiativeLabelCreate
fields.description: Creates a workspace label or label group for initiatives. Requires workspace label-management permission. Use parentId to place a label in a group.

args.name: input
args.description: The initiative label to create.

fields.name: initiativeLabelDelete
fields.description: Deletes an initiative label and its children, removing their assignments from initiatives.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to delete.

fields.name: initiativeLabelRestore
fields.description: Restores a previously retired initiative label, making it available for use on new initiatives.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to restore.

fields.name: initiativeLabelRetire
fields.description: Retires an initiative label. Retired labels remain on existing initiatives but cannot be applied to new ones.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to retire.

fields.name: initiativeLabelUpdate
fields.description: Changes the supplied label fields. Omitted fields stay unchanged. Requires workspace label-management permission.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial label object to update.

fields.name: initiativeRelationCreate
fields.description: Adds a child initiative to a parent. Both must be accessible and unarchived, and the workspace must support sub-initiatives. When the new parent overlaps the child’s existing hierarchy, the overlapping parent links are removed as part of the move. Cycles and excessive nesting are rejected.

args.name: input
args.description: The initiative relation to create.

fields.name: initiativeRelationDelete
fields.description: Removes a parent-child link without deleting either initiative. Deleting a link that no longer exists succeeds without making changes; an existing link still requires access to both initiatives.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative relation to delete.

fields.name: initiativeRelationUpdate
fields.description: Changes a child initiative’s ordering within its parent. The relation’s endpoints remain unchanged. Both initiatives must be visible to you.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative relation to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the initiative relation to update.

fields.name: initiativeRemoveLabel
fields.description: Removes a label from the initiative while keeping its other labels. The label itself is not deleted.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative to remove the label from.

args.name: labelId
args.description: The identifier of the label to remove.

fields.name: initiativeToProjectCreate
fields.description: Links an accessible, active project to an accessible, active initiative. Neither may be read-only. The link is rejected if the project is already in that initiative or one of its ancestors or descendants. App users need initiative:write scope.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the initiativeToProject to create.

fields.name: initiativeToProjectDelete
fields.description: Removes an active project-to-initiative link without deleting either entity. Requires access to the association; app users need initiative:write scope.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiativeToProject to delete.

fields.name: initiativeToProjectUpdate
fields.description: Changes the project’s sort order within the initiative. The initiative and project endpoints cannot be changed through this mutation.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiativeToProject to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the initiativeToProject to update.

fields.name: initiativeUnarchive
fields.description: Restores an archived or trashed initiative. This makes the existing initiative available again with its saved properties and associations.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative to unarchive.

fields.name: initiativeUpdate
fields.description: Updates the supplied fields of an initiative you can access. Omitted fields keep their current values. Changing the lead team can change who can see the initiative, and the owner must be able to access the new team.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the initiative to update.

fields.name: initiativeUpdateArchive
fields.description: Archives an update and recalculates the initiative’s health from the remaining updates. You must be the author or have permission to manage workspace entities. Use initiativeUpdateUnarchive to restore it.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative update to archive.

fields.name: initiativeUpdateCreate
fields.description: Publishes an update, records the current user as author, captures the initiative’s projects, and refreshes its health. Provide the written message in input.body.

args.name: input
args.description: The initiative update object to create.

fields.name: initiativeUpdateUnarchive
fields.description: Restores an archived update and recalculates the initiative’s health. You must be the author or have permission to manage workspace entities.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative update to unarchive.

fields.name: initiativeUpdateUpdate
fields.description: Edits an update’s message or health. You must be the author or have permission to manage workspace entities. Editing the latest update while it is less than one hour old also refreshes its project snapshots.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the initiative update to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the initiative update to update.

fields.name: integrationArchive
fields.description: Disconnects an integration that supports archiving while retaining its record for a later reconnect. You can archive your own personal connection; workspace connections generally require integration-creation permission. GitHub installation removal and Jira webhook cleanup run in the background, so a successful response can precede the completed disconnection. Services that do not support archiving must use integrationDelete instead.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the integration to archive.

fields.name: integrationAsksConnectChannel
fields.description: Connects the public or private Slack channel selected during OAuth to an existing Asks integration. The channel must be in that integration's Slack workspace and must not already be connected. Individual channel connections require full Asks access and permission to manage Asks settings. Check addBot after success and invite the bot manually when true. Direct messages work with Asks without this setup.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationDelete
fields.description: Disconnects an integration that supports deletion and removes its connection record. You can remove your own personal connection; workspace connections require integration-creation permission, and team, project, or view connections follow the permissions for that resource. Some services finish external cleanup in the background, so success does not guarantee that cleanup has finished. Services that retain a record for reconnecting must use integrationArchive instead.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the integration to delete.

args.name: skipInstallationDeletion
args.description: Whether to skip deleting the installation on the external service side.

fields.name: integrationDiscord
fields.description: Connects a Discord server using the OAuth code and redirect URI from its authorization flow, and links the authorizing Discord user to your Linear account. A Linear workspace can have one Discord connection, and the Discord server cannot already belong to another Linear workspace's connection.

args.name: code
args.description: The Discord OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Discord OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationFigma
fields.description: Connects Figma using an OAuth authorization code and its redirect URI, storing the credentials needed for the workspace integration. The workspace cannot already have an active Figma connection.

args.name: code
args.description: The Figma OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Figma OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationFront
fields.description: Connects Front using an OAuth grant. Requires the workspace's support integration plan feature and no existing Front connection. New connections initially reopen linked Front conversations when a Linear issue is completed or canceled; comments do not trigger reopening by default.

args.name: code
args.description: The Front OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Front OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationGitHubEnterpriseServerConnect
fields.description: Starts a GitHub Enterprise Server connection for a GitHub organization or personal account. Open setupUrl to register the app, configure it with webhookSecret, then use installUrl to install it. Call verifyGitHubEnterpriseServerInstallation to check that the app has connected. Success here means the setup record was saved, not that installation is complete. An archived connection for the same organization is reused.

args.name: githubUrl
args.description: The base URL of the GitHub Enterprise Server installation.

args.name: organizationName
args.description: GitHub organization login name. Use an empty string to create the app for a personal account.

fields.name: integrationGitHubPersonal
fields.description: Links your GitHub account using an OAuth code from Linear's GitHub App authorization flow. codeAccess selects the app with repository code access and defaults to false. This is a personal account connection; connecting a workspace's GitHub App installation uses integrationGithubConnect.

args.name: code
args.description: The GitHub OAuth code.

args.name: codeAccess
args.description: Whether to connect with code access.

args.name: enterpriseUrl
args.description: The enterprise URL for GitHub Enterprise Cloud connections. Omit for github.com.

fields.name: integrationGithubCommitCreate
fields.description: Creates the workspace's GitHub commit integration and returns its webhook secret. Use the secret when configuring the webhook in GitHub; creating this record alone does not configure GitHub to send events.

fields.name: integrationGithubConnect
fields.description: Connects a GitHub App installation to the workspace using its installation ID and OAuth grant. If replacing a connection would make repositories used by GitHub Issues sync inaccessible, the call stops and returns gitHub.lostRepositoryNames. Review that list, then repeat with confirmReplace set to true to accept the change. GitHub Enterprise Cloud connections require the corresponding workspace plan feature.

args.name: code
args.description: The GitHub grant code that's exchanged for OAuth tokens.

args.name: codeAccess
args.description: Whether to connect the GitHub App with repository code access. Defaults to false.

args.name: confirmReplace
args.description: Confirm replacing an existing installation after a prior call reported lostRepositoryNames. Defaults to false.

args.name: githubHost
args.description: GitHub Enterprise Cloud hostname, such as acme.ghe.com, without a URL scheme or path. Omit for github.com.

args.name: installationId
args.description: GitHub App installation ID as a positive integer string.

fields.name: integrationGithubImportConnect
fields.description: Connects the GitHub Import App installation authorized by the supplied OAuth code. This creates the connection used to discover repositories for import; it does not import issues by itself.

args.name: code
args.description: The GitHub grant code that's exchanged for OAuth tokens.

args.name: installationId
args.description: GitHub App installation ID as a positive integer string.

fields.name: integrationGithubImportRefresh
fields.description: Queues a refresh of repositories and labels available to a GitHub import integration. Success confirms scheduling.

args.name: id
args.description: The id of the integration to update.

fields.name: integrationGithubRemoveCodeAccess
fields.description: Removes repository code access from a GitHub connection. Check action in the response: Done means the change is complete, while InstallBasicApp means you need to finish installing the basic GitHub App before setup is complete.

args.name: integrationId
args.description: The ID of the integration to remove code access from.

fields.name: integrationGitlabConnect
fields.description: Connects a GitLab instance after checking its access token. Configure the GitLab webhook with the returned webhookSecret after a successful response. Only one GitLab connection is allowed per workspace. Token or connectivity failures return success=false and diagnostic error fields instead of creating a connection.

args.name: accessToken
args.description: GitLab access token for the instance being connected. Linear validates it before saving the connection and uses its reported scopes and expiry when available.

args.name: expiresAt
args.description: ISO timestamp when the access token expires. Used as a fallback when `validationProjectPath` is set and `personal_access_tokens/self` is unreachable.

args.name: gitlabUrl
args.description: Base URL of the GitLab instance, including its URL scheme. Linear uses this host for token validation and subsequent API requests.

args.name: readonly
args.description: Whether the access token is limited to a read-only scope. Used as a fallback when `validationProjectPath` is set and `personal_access_tokens/self` is unreachable.

args.name: validationProjectPath
args.description: Optional path or numeric ID of a project to use for the setup health check. Set this when the GitLab tenant blocks non-project API endpoints.

fields.name: integrationGitlabRotate
fields.description: Rotates the GitLab token, revoking the previous token and saving its replacement.

args.name: integrationId
args.description: UUID of the GitLab integration.

fields.name: integrationGitlabTestConnection
fields.description: Tests the stored access token against a self-hosted GitLab instance, using the validation project when one is configured. A successful check clears the connection's authentication and transient failure state. On failure, inspect success and the error fields for provider or proxy diagnostics. This mutation does not support the GitLab.com OAuth connection.

args.name: integrationId
args.description: The ID of the GitLab integration to test.

fields.name: integrationGitlabUpdateRotationSettings
fields.description: Enables or disables automatic self-rotation of the GitLab token.

args.name: enabled
args.description: Whether Linear should automatically rotate the GitLab token.

args.name: integrationId
args.description: UUID of the GitLab integration.

fields.name: integrationGitlabUpdateToken
fields.description: Replaces a GitLab integration's access token after validating the replacement against its existing host and validation project. The connection and webhook stay in place. Supply readonly and expiresAt when the instance cannot report that token information.

args.name: accessToken
args.description: Replacement GitLab access token. Validated before it replaces the current token.

args.name: expiresAt
args.description: The time at which the replacement token expires. Used when GitLab cannot return its expiry.

args.name: integrationId
args.description: UUID of the GitLab integration.

args.name: readonly
args.description: Whether the replacement token has read-only access. Required when GitLab cannot return its scopes.

fields.name: integrationGong
fields.description: Connects Gong using an OAuth authorization code and its redirect URI. Requires the workspace's Gong integration plan feature and integration-creation permission. The workspace cannot already have an active Gong connection.

args.name: code
args.description: The Gong OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Gong OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationGoogleSheets
fields.description: Connects Google Sheets using an OAuth grant that includes both access and refresh tokens. The workspace can have one active Google Sheets connection. This call saves the connection; use refreshGoogleSheetsData to request an export refresh.

args.name: code
args.description: The Google OAuth code.

fields.name: integrationIntercom
fields.description: Connects an Intercom workspace using an OAuth code and the redirect URI used during authorization. The workspace needs access to the support integration plan feature. Reconnecting the same Intercom workspace refreshes credentials and keeps its settings; disconnect first to switch to a different Intercom workspace. An Intercom workspace cannot be connected to another Linear workspace at the same time.

args.name: code
args.description: The Intercom OAuth code.

args.name: domainUrl
args.description: The Intercom domain URL to use for the integration. Defaults to app.intercom.com if not provided.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Intercom OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationIntercomDelete
fields.description: Uninstalls the Intercom connection and removes its Linear record. It also completes local cleanup when access was already revoked in Intercom. Calling this after the Linear connection has been removed returns an error.

fields.name: integrationIntercomSettingsUpdate
fields.description: [DEPRECATED] Updates settings on the Intercom integration.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial Intercom integration settings object to update the integration settings with.

fields.deprecationReason: Manage Intercom integration settings in Linear workspace settings.

fields.name: integrationJiraPersonal
fields.description: Links your Jira account to an existing workspace Jira integration. Supply either the OAuth authorization code for Jira Cloud or a personal access token for Jira Server. When the workspace has more than one possible Jira connection, supply workspaceIntegrationId to choose which one to link.

args.name: accessToken
args.description: The Jira personal access token, when connecting using a PAT.

args.name: code
args.description: The Jira OAuth code, when connecting using OAuth.

args.name: workspaceIntegrationId
args.description: The workspace Jira integration to connect to. Required when the connection would otherwise be ambiguous.

fields.name: integrationLoom
fields.description: Enables Loom integration for the workspace.

fields.name: integrationMicrosoftPersonalConnect
fields.description: Links your Microsoft account to Linear. Its tenant must already be connected through a workspace Microsoft Teams integration. Reconnecting the same account refreshes credentials when the existing personal connection has an authentication error; otherwise, disconnect the existing personal connection before linking another account.

args.name: code
args.description: The Microsoft OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Microsoft OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationMicrosoftTeams
fields.description: Connects the Microsoft tenant identified by the OAuth grant to this Linear workspace. An archived connection to the same tenant is restored. Multiple tenants require the corresponding plan feature, and a tenant cannot be actively connected to another Linear workspace. Personal Microsoft accounts are linked separately with integrationMicrosoftPersonalConnect.

args.name: code
args.description: The Microsoft OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Microsoft OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationRequest
fields.description: Records interest in an integration that is not currently available. No authentication is required, and this does not create an integration or start an installation. Success means the request was accepted for analytics; it does not promise that the integration will be built.

args.name: input
args.description: Integration request details.

fields.name: integrationSalesforce
fields.description: Connects Salesforce using an OAuth grant and verifies that the authorizing user can access the Linear managed package, including its required license. Requires the workspace's enterprise integration plan feature. Reconnecting an active connection to the same subdomain refreshes credentials while keeping settings and templates; restoring an archived connection runs setup again. Disconnect first to switch to a different Salesforce subdomain.

args.name: code
args.description: The Salesforce OAuth code.

args.name: codeVerifier
args.description: The PKCE code verifier matching the code_challenge sent on authorization.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Salesforce OAuth redirect URI.

args.name: subdomain
args.description: Salesforce installation subdomain. Use the subdomain alone, containing letters, numbers, and dashes, rather than a complete URL.

fields.name: integrationSentryConnect
fields.description: Connects a Sentry installation by exchanging its grant code and confirming installation with Sentry. The workspace can have one active Sentry connection. The new connection initially enables completing linked Linear issues when Sentry issues are resolved and reopening them when Sentry issues are unresolved.

args.name: code
args.description: The Sentry grant code that's exchanged for OAuth tokens.

args.name: installationId
args.description: The Sentry installationId to connect with.

args.name: organizationSlug
args.description: The slug of the Sentry organization being connected.

fields.name: integrationSlack
fields.description: Connects a Slack workspace to the main Linear Slack app using an OAuth grant. Reconnecting an archived connection restores it with fresh credentials. Connecting multiple Slack workspaces requires the corresponding plan feature; the same Slack workspace cannot have two active connections or belong to another Linear workspace's connection.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

args.name: requestedScopes
args.description: The Slack OAuth scopes the client requested. Used to warn when Slack grants fewer scopes than requested.

args.name: shouldUseV2Auth
args.description: [DEPRECATED] Whether or not v2 of Slack OAuth should be used. No longer used.

fields.name: integrationSlackAsks
fields.description: Connects a Slack workspace to the Linear Asks app for issue intake. Requires a workspace plan with Asks access. An archived connection to the same Slack workspace is restored with fresh credentials. Multiple Slack workspaces require the corresponding plan feature, and each Slack workspace can be connected to Asks in only one Linear workspace.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

args.name: requestedScopes
args.description: The Slack OAuth scopes the client requested. Used to warn when Slack grants fewer scopes than requested.

fields.name: integrationSlackCustomViewNotifications
fields.description: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to a custom view and creates default notification settings if needed. You must be able to edit the view, and the view cannot already have this type of Slack connection. Check the response for remaining bot or workspace setup.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: customViewId
args.description: UUID of the Linear custom view whose notifications should be sent to the selected Slack channel.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationSlackCustomerChannelLink
fields.description: Links a customer to a public or private Slack channel in a connected Asks workspace. Both the customer and channel must be unlinked.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: customerId
args.description: The customer to link the Slack channel with

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationSlackImportEmojis
fields.description: Queues an import of custom emoji from Slack using the OAuth grant. Success confirms scheduling.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationSlackOrAsksUpdateSlackTeamName
fields.description: Fetches the current Slack workspace name and updates the name stored on an active Slack or Asks integration. This refreshes Linear's display name; it does not rename the workspace in Slack. A valid integration token is required.

args.name: integrationId
args.description: The integration ID.

fields.name: integrationSlackOrgProjectUpdatesPost
fields.description: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to receive project updates from across the workspace. Requires integration-management permission. Check addBot and the nudge fields in the response for any remaining Slack setup.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationSlackPersonal
fields.description: Links your Slack account for personal notifications and opens a direct message with the Linear app. The Slack workspace must already have a Slack or Asks connection. You can have one active personal Slack connection, and the same Slack account cannot be linked to another user in this Linear workspace. An archived connection owned by you can be restored.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: integrationSlackPost
fields.description: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to a Linear team and creates its default notification settings if needed. Requires permission to manage the team, and each team can have one such connection. Direct messages are not supported. Check addBot and the nudge fields in the response for any remaining Slack setup.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

args.name: shouldUseV2Auth
args.description: [DEPRECATED] Whether or not v2 of Slack OAuth should be used. No longer used.

args.name: teamId
args.description: UUID of the Linear team whose notifications should be sent to the selected Slack channel. This is not a Slack workspace or channel ID.

fields.name: integrationSlackProjectPost
fields.description: Connects the Slack channel selected during OAuth to a project you can access. Choose notifications for project notifications or updates for project updates; each service can have one connection per project. The call also links the channel to the project and creates default notification settings if needed. Check the response for remaining bot or workspace setup.

args.name: code
args.description: The Slack OAuth code.

args.name: projectId
args.description: UUID of the Linear project whose notifications or updates should be sent to the selected Slack channel.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Slack OAuth redirect URI.

args.name: service
args.description: The service to enable once connected, either 'notifications' or 'updates'.

fields.name: integrationTemplateCreate
fields.description: Makes an issue template available through Slack Asks, Slack, Intercom, Zendesk, or Salesforce. Slack Asks requires permission to manage Asks, a connected intake destination, and a team template; linking the template enables triage for that team. Other supported integrations require integration-management permission and accept up to ten templates. Private-team templates are supported only by Slack Asks.

args.name: input
args.description: The template, integration, and optional external resource to link.

fields.name: integrationTemplateDelete
fields.description: Removes a template's link to an integration or intake destination. The template itself and the integration remain available. Requires permission to manage the Asks integration for Slack Asks, or integration-management permission for other services.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the template-integration link to delete.

fields.name: integrationZendesk
fields.description: Connects Zendesk using an OAuth grant and creates or selects the user that authors internal notes. Requires the workspace's support integration plan feature. Reconnecting the same subdomain refreshes credentials and keeps existing settings; an archived connection is restored. Disconnect the current integration before switching to a different Zendesk subdomain.

args.name: accessToken
args.description: Bearer token that authenticates API requests instead of a Zendesk OAuth token. Requires `customApiUrl`; no OAuth exchange is performed.

args.name: botUserId
args.description: The Zendesk user ID to use as the author of internal notes instead of creating a bot user. Omit to keep the configured user on reconnect, or pass null to create a new bot user.

args.name: botUserRole
args.description: Role for the Zendesk bot user Linear creates: end-user or agent. Omit to retain the role on reconnect; new connections default to end-user. Ignored when botUserId selects an existing user.

args.name: code
args.description: The Zendesk OAuth authorization code.

args.name: customApiUrl
args.description: Custom base URL for Zendesk API requests, such as a proxy in front of Zendesk. OAuth requests always use the standard subdomain URL.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Zendesk OAuth redirect URI. Required when connecting with `code`.

args.name: scope
args.description: The Zendesk OAuth scopes. Required when connecting with `code`.

args.name: subdomain
args.description: Zendesk subdomain, such as acme for acme.zendesk.com. Use letters, numbers, and dashes without a scheme or domain suffix.

fields.name: integrationsSettingsCreate
fields.description: Creates notification preferences for a destination you can access, with edit permission required for custom views. Supply exactly one team, project, initiative, or view. Settings must not already exist for that destination and, for team settings, context view; use integrationsSettingsUpdate when they do. An app writing initiative preferences also needs initiative:write scope.

args.name: input
args.description: The settings to create.

fields.name: integrationsSettingsUpdate
fields.description: Updates the event preferences on an existing integration settings record. Only supplied booleans change, and the destination stays the same. Custom-view settings require permission to edit the view; apps changing initiative settings need initiative:write scope. For older settings that combined update and comment notifications, the first edit preserves the previous comment preference independently.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the settings to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A settings object to update the settings with.

fields.name: issueAddLabel
fields.description: Add a label without replacing the issue’s existing labels. The label must be available to the issue’s team.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to add the label to.

args.name: labelId
args.description: The identifier of the label to add.

fields.name: issueArchive
fields.description: Archives an issue and its sub-issues, keeping their data available for later restoration. Archived issues are excluded from normal issue lists. Pass trash only when you want the deletion grace period to apply instead.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to archive.

args.name: trash
args.description: Whether to trash the issue and its sub-issues.

fields.name: issueBatchCreate
fields.description: Creates one to 50 issues in a single batch. If any creation fails, none of the issues in the batch are saved. Put parent inputs before their sub-issues and supply parent UUIDs to connect issues created in the same batch.

args.name: input
args.description: A list of issue objects to create.

fields.name: issueBatchUpdate
fields.description: Applies the same update input to one to 50 issues. The batch runs as one transaction, so a failed update rolls back the other updates. Use the returned issues to read the resulting values.

args.name: ids
args.description: One to 50 distinct issue UUIDs to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial issue object to update the issues with.

fields.name: issueCreate
fields.description: Creates an issue in the chosen team and returns it with its assigned identifier. You can supply a template to populate defaults and create any sub-issues it defines. Team settings and automation may set values such as the initial status, assignee, and cycle.

args.name: input
args.description: The issue object to create.

fields.name: issueDelete
fields.description: Moves an issue to the trash and trashes its unarchived sub-issues that you can access. Trashed issues can be restored during the 30-day grace period; permanentlyDelete skips that period and requires workspace entity-management permission.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to delete.

args.name: permanentlyDelete
args.description: Delete immediately, skipping the 30-day grace period. Requires workspace permission to manage entities and access to the issue’s team.

fields.name: issueExternalSyncDisable
fields.description: Stop syncing an issue with the Jira or GitHub integration identified by its sync attachment.

args.name: attachmentId
args.description: The ID of the sync attachment to disable.

fields.name: issueImportCreateAsana
fields.description: Starts fetching Asana tasks into an asynchronous import job. Choose an existing destination team or a new team name. Configure the fetched data and call issueImportProcess to create Linear records.

args.name: asanaProjectNames
args.description: Names of Asana projects in the team. When set, only tasks from these projects are imported. When empty, all projects are imported.

args.name: asanaTeamName
args.description: Name of the source Asana team.

args.name: asanaToken
args.description: Asana token to fetch information from the Asana API.

args.name: id
args.description: ID of issue import. If not provided it will be generated.

args.name: includeClosedIssues
args.description: Include completed Asana tasks when fetching source data.

args.name: instantProcess
args.description: Start creating Linear records after fetching source data, using default mappings. Defaults to false, allowing mappings to be reviewed first.

args.name: teamId
args.description: UUID of an existing destination team. Provide either teamId or teamName.

args.name: teamName
args.description: Name of a new destination team. Provide either teamId or teamName.

fields.name: issueImportCreateCSVJira
fields.description: Creates an asynchronous import from a Jira CSV already uploaded to the workspace’s import storage. Choose an existing destination team or a new team name. The response accepts the job; it does not mean the imported records are ready.

args.name: csvUrl
args.description: Asset URL of a Jira CSV uploaded to this workspace’s import storage.

args.name: jiraEmail
args.description: Jira user account email.

args.name: jiraHostname
args.description: Jira installation or cloud hostname.

args.name: jiraToken
args.description: Jira personal access token to access Jira REST API.

args.name: teamId
args.description: UUID of an existing destination team. To create a team, omit this and provide teamName.

args.name: teamName
args.description: Name of a new destination team. Cannot be combined with teamId.

fields.name: issueImportCreateClubhouse
fields.description: Starts fetching stories from Shortcut, whose legacy API name is clubhouse, into an asynchronous import job. Choose an existing destination team or a new team name. Configure the fetched data and call issueImportProcess to create Linear records.

args.name: clubhouseGroupName
args.description: Name of the source Shortcut group.

args.name: clubhouseToken
args.description: Shortcut (formerly Clubhouse) token to fetch information from the Clubhouse API.

args.name: id
args.description: ID of issue import. If not provided it will be generated.

args.name: includeClosedIssues
args.description: Include completed Shortcut stories when fetching source data.

args.name: instantProcess
args.description: Start creating Linear records after fetching source data, using default mappings. Defaults to false, allowing mappings to be reviewed first.

args.name: teamId
args.description: UUID of an existing destination team. Provide either teamId or teamName.

args.name: teamName
args.description: Name of a new destination team. Provide either teamId or teamName.

fields.name: issueImportCreateGithub
fields.description: Starts fetching GitHub issues into an asynchronous import job. Choose an existing destination team or provide a name for a new one, and repositories the workspace can import from. After fetching and configuration, use issueImportProcess to create the Linear records. Requires workspace import permission.

args.name: githubLabels
args.description: GitHub label names to use when filtering the imported issues. Omit or send an empty list to import without a label filter.

args.name: githubRepoIds
args.description: Numeric GitHub repository IDs to import. The workspace must have import access to these repositories.

args.name: includeClosedIssues
args.description: Include closed GitHub issues when fetching source data.

args.name: instantProcess
args.description: Start creating Linear records after fetching source data, using default mappings. Defaults to false, allowing mappings to be reviewed first.

args.name: teamId
args.description: UUID of an existing destination team. Provide either teamId or teamName.

args.name: teamName
args.description: Name of a new destination team. Provide either teamId or teamName.

fields.name: issueImportCreateJira
fields.description: Starts fetching Jira issues into an asynchronous import job. Choose an existing destination team or a new team name and the source Jira project. After fetching and configuration, use issueImportProcess to create the Linear records. Requires workspace import permission.

args.name: id
args.description: ID of issue import. If not provided it will be generated.

args.name: includeClosedIssues
args.description: Include closed Jira issues when fetching source data.

args.name: instantProcess
args.description: Start creating Linear records after fetching source data, using default mappings. Defaults to false, allowing mappings to be reviewed first.

args.name: jiraEmail
args.description: Jira user account email.

args.name: jiraHostname
args.description: Jira installation or cloud hostname.

args.name: jiraProject
args.description: Jira project key from which we will import data.

args.name: jiraToken
args.description: Jira personal access token to access Jira REST API.

args.name: jql
args.description: Additional JQL conditions within jiraProject. The project restriction is always applied.

args.name: teamId
args.description: UUID of an existing destination team. Provide either teamId or teamName.

args.name: teamName
args.description: Name of a new destination team. Provide either teamId or teamName.

fields.name: issueImportDelete
fields.description: Schedules deletion of an import and the data it created, then returns the job with status deleting. This is available within 14 days for eligible imports awaiting configuration, completed imports, or failed imports. You must be the creator or an admin with the destination team’s deletion permission, and another import from the same service must not be processing.

args.name: issueImportId
args.description: ID of the issue import to delete.

fields.name: issueImportProcess
fields.description: Saves the supplied mappings and schedules creation of Linear records from the fetched source data. The import must be inProgress; otherwise the mappings are saved but success is false. A successful response means processing was accepted, not that it has finished. Linear-to-Linear migrations can only be managed from the Linear app.

args.name: issueImportId
args.description: ID of the issue import which we're going to process.

args.name: mapping
args.description: The mapping configuration to use for processing the import.

fields.name: issueImportUpdate
fields.description: Saves mapping choices without starting the import. For external-service imports, supply the full replacement mapping. Requires workspace import permission; Linear-to-Linear migrations can only be managed from the Linear app.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue import.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the issue import to update.

fields.name: issueLabelCreate
fields.description: Create a workspace or team label. Requires permission to manage labels in its scope.

args.name: input
args.description: The issue label to create.

args.name: replaceTeamLabels
args.description: Whether to replace all team-specific labels with the same name with this newly created workspace label (default: false).

fields.name: issueLabelDelete
fields.description: Deletes a label and its inherited copies. Assignments to that label are removed from issues in the background, so they may remain visible briefly after the mutation succeeds. Retire a label instead if you want to preserve its existing assignments.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to delete.

fields.name: issueLabelRestore
fields.description: Makes a retired label available for new assignments again. Existing issue assignments are preserved. Restoring a group also restores its child labels.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to restore.

fields.name: issueLabelRetire
fields.description: Retires a label so it cannot be newly assigned, while keeping it on issues that already use it. Retiring a group also retires its children. Use issueLabelRestore to make the label available again.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to retire.

fields.name: issueLabelUpdate
fields.description: Update a label. Requires permission to manage labels in its scope; inherited labels must be edited at their source.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial label object to update.

args.name: replaceTeamLabels
args.description: Whether to replace all team-specific labels with the same name with this updated workspace label (default: false).

fields.name: issueRelationCreate
fields.description: Creates a relationship between two issues, replacing any conflicting relation between the pair and reusing an identical one. A duplicate relation closes the source as a duplicate of the target and can move linked customer requests to the target. You must have access to both issues and any permissions required for the merge.

args.name: input
args.description: The issue relation to create.

args.name: overrideCreatedAt
args.description: Used by client undo operations. Should not be set directly.

fields.name: issueRelationDelete
fields.description: Removes a relation by its UUID. Removing a duplicate relation also runs the unmerge behavior, including moving customer requests back to the original issue when applicable.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue relation to delete.

fields.name: issueRelationUpdate
fields.description: Changes a relation’s type or the issues it connects. Omitted fields are unchanged, and an issue cannot relate to itself. Changing to or from duplicate also applies the corresponding merge or unmerge behavior.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue relation to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the issue relation to update.

fields.name: issueReminder
fields.description: Creates a reminder notification for you at reminderAt. The time must be in the future, and existing reminders for this issue are replaced. The payload returns success without an issue object.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to add a reminder for.

args.name: reminderAt
args.description: Future time at which to deliver the reminder notification.

fields.name: issueRemoveLabel
fields.description: Remove one label while keeping the issue’s other labels.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to remove the label from.

args.name: labelId
args.description: The identifier of the label to remove.

fields.name: issueShare
fields.description: Shares an issue with a user who would not otherwise be able to access it. The viewer must have native access to the issue's full sub-issue tree and permission to share issues in the issue's team. Issues that inherit sharing from a parent issue cannot be shared directly.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to share.

args.name: userId
args.description: The identifier of the user to share the issue with.

fields.name: issueSubscribe
fields.description: Subscribes a user to issue updates. Omit both userId and userEmail to subscribe yourself, or provide one of them to choose another workspace user. Subscribing an existing subscriber leaves the subscription in place.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to subscribe to.

args.name: userEmail
args.description: Email of an active workspace user to subscribe. Cannot be combined with userId.

args.name: userId
args.description: UUID of the user to subscribe. Cannot be combined with userEmail.

fields.name: issueToReleaseCreate
fields.description: Associates an issue with a release and returns the link. The issue must be editable and both resources accessible; release management must be available in the workspace. If the association already exists, the mutation returns an error rather than reusing it.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the issueToRelease to create.

fields.name: issueToReleaseDelete
fields.description: Removes an issue-to-release association by the link’s UUID, keeping the issue and release. The issue must be editable and the release accessible. Returns an error when the link does not exist.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue-to-release association to delete.

fields.name: issueToReleaseDeleteByIssueAndRelease
fields.description: Removes the association between the specified issue and release, keeping both resources. The issue must be editable and the release accessible. Returns an error when the association does not exist.

args.name: issueId
args.description: The identifier of the issue. Can be a UUID or issue identifier (e.g., 'LIN-123').

args.name: releaseId
args.description: The identifier of the release.

fields.name: issueUnarchive
fields.description: Restores an archived issue and its sub-issues to normal issue lists. Automatic-archive markers are cleared, and a project association is removed if the project no longer includes the issue’s team.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to unarchive.

fields.name: issueUnshare
fields.description: Stops sharing an issue with a user. The viewer must have native access to the issue's full sub-issue tree and permission to share issues in the issue's team. Issues that inherit sharing from a parent issue cannot be unshared directly.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to stop sharing.

args.name: userId
args.description: The identifier of the user to remove from the issue share.

fields.name: issueUnsubscribe
fields.description: Removes a user’s subscription to issue updates. Omit both userId and userEmail to unsubscribe yourself, or provide one of them to choose another workspace user.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to unsubscribe from.

args.name: userEmail
args.description: Email of an active workspace user to unsubscribe. Cannot be combined with userId.

args.name: userId
args.description: UUID of the user to unsubscribe. Cannot be combined with userEmail.

fields.name: issueUpdate
fields.description: Updates an issue by UUID or human-readable identifier and returns its resulting values. Omitted fields keep their values; list inputs replace their existing lists unless an add/remove field is used. Changes can also trigger team workflow behavior, such as automatic cycle assignment.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the issue to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial issue object to update the issue with.

fields.name: jiraProjectBatchMigrate
fields.description: Imports or syncs up to 50 projects from one connected Jira site. When both are requested, sync starts after import. Projects are checked independently; retry failed projects only. Repeating an unchanged, running migration returns its existing records. Imports into one team run sequentially. Requires the `admin` scope, access to destination teams, and import permission when importing.

args.name: input
args.description: The Jira projects to migrate.

fields.name: logout
fields.description: Signs out the current session and clears authentication cookies. If the token has no session ID, signs out all sessions for the account.

args.name: reason
args.description: Optional reason recorded with the sign-out event. It does not change which sessions are revoked.

fields.name: logoutAllSessions
fields.description: Signs out all sessions for the account, including the current session, and clears authentication cookies.

args.name: reason
args.description: Optional reason recorded with the sign-out event. It does not change which sessions are revoked.

fields.name: logoutOtherSessions
fields.description: Signs out every other session for the authenticated account while keeping the current session active.

args.name: reason
args.description: Optional reason recorded with the sign-out event. It does not change which sessions are revoked.

fields.name: logoutSession
fields.description: Revokes one sign-in session belonging to the authenticated account. Use an ID returned by authenticationSessions; it may be the current session or another device's session. Requires session JWT authentication.

args.name: sessionId
args.description: ID of the session to logout.

fields.name: notificationArchive
fields.description: Archives one of your notifications, removing it from the active inbox. Other notifications in the same group remain unchanged. Use notificationArchiveAll to archive the group.

args.name: id
args.description: The id of the notification to archive.

fields.name: notificationArchiveAll
fields.description: Archives the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group.

args.name: input
args.description: The entity or notification group whose notifications to change. Supply exactly one identifier.

fields.name: notificationCategoryChannelSubscriptionUpdate
fields.description: Subscribes to or unsubscribes from a specific notification category for a given notification channel. For example, subscribe to 'issueAssignment' notifications via the 'email' channel.

args.name: category
args.description: The notification category to subscribe to or unsubscribe from

args.name: channel
args.description: The notification channel in which to subscribe to or unsubscribe from the category

args.name: subscribe
args.description: True if the user wants to subscribe, false if the user wants to unsubscribe

fields.name: notificationMarkReadAll
fields.description: Marks the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group as read.

args.name: input
args.description: The entity or notification group whose notifications to change. Supply exactly one identifier.

args.name: readAt
args.description: The time when notification was marked as read.

fields.name: notificationMarkUnreadAll
fields.description: Marks the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group as unread.

args.name: input
args.description: The entity or notification group whose notifications to change. Supply exactly one identifier.

fields.name: notificationSnoozeAll
fields.description: Snoozes the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group.

args.name: input
args.description: The entity or notification group whose notifications to change. Supply exactly one identifier.

args.name: snoozedUntilAt
args.description: The time until a notification will be snoozed. After that it will appear in the inbox again.

fields.name: notificationSubscriptionCreate
fields.description: Subscribes the authenticated user to one target and its requested notification types. Rejects an existing subscription to the same target and view.

args.name: input
args.description: The subscription object to create.

fields.name: notificationSubscriptionDelete
fields.description: Deletes a notification subscription reference.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the notification subscription reference to delete.

fields.name: notificationSubscriptionUpdate
fields.description: Updates a subscription owned by the authenticated user. Use active: false to pause it without deleting its configuration, or replace notificationSubscriptionTypes to change the events you follow. Subscriptions to read-only projects cannot be changed.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the notification subscription to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial notification subscription object to update the notification subscription with.

fields.name: notificationUnarchive
fields.description: Restores one of your archived notifications. Its read and snooze states are preserved, so a snoozed notification may still be absent from the visible inbox.

args.name: id
args.description: The id of the notification to unarchive.

fields.name: notificationUnsnoozeAll
fields.description: Unsnoozes the authenticated user’s active notifications for the selected entity or notification group.

args.name: input
args.description: The entity or notification group whose notifications to change. Supply exactly one identifier.

args.name: unsnoozedAt
args.description: The time when the notification was unsnoozed.

fields.name: notificationUpdate
fields.description: Updates one of the authenticated user’s notifications. Related notifications are unchanged.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the notification to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial notification object to update the notification with.

fields.name: oauthApplicationArchive
fields.description: [ALPHA] Archives an OAuth application created by the calling OAuth application.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the OAuth application to archive.

fields.name: oauthApplicationCreate
fields.description: [ALPHA] Creates an OAuth application private to the current workspace and managed by the calling OAuth application. The caller needs workspace API management permission. Save clientSecret and any webhookSecret from the first successful response. Retrying with the same idempotency key returns the existing unarchived application without updating it and with secrets omitted. Use the application’s id for later management operations and clientId for OAuth flows.

args.name: input
args.description: The OAuth application object to create.

fields.name: oauthApplicationRotateSecret
fields.description: [ALPHA] Replaces the client secret for an application created by the caller and returns the new secret. Store it before discarding the response; it cannot be retrieved later. Tokens issued through client_credentials are revoked, while tokens from the authorization-code flow remain valid. The caller must be able to manage the application’s credentials, including its private-team access, as well as have workspace API management permission.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the OAuth application for which to rotate the secret.

fields.name: oauthApplicationRotateWebhookSecret
fields.description: [ALPHA] Rotates the webhook signing secret for an OAuth application created by the calling OAuth application.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the OAuth application for which to rotate the webhook secret.

fields.name: oauthApplicationUpdate
fields.description: [ALPHA] Updates an unarchived application created by the calling OAuth application in this workspace. Omitted fields keep their current values. Enabling client_credentials or changing the webhook destination requires access to every private team available to the app, or workspace owner permission; an app with access to all private teams requires an owner. Workspace API management permission is required for every update.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the OAuth application to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial OAuth application object to update.

fields.name: organizationCancelDelete
fields.description: Cancels a scheduled workspace deletion while the deletion process still permits cancellation. Requires workspace-settings permission.

fields.name: organizationDelete
fields.description: Schedules deletion of the workspace and its data after validating the code from organizationDeleteChallenge. This does not finish the deletion during the request. Use organizationCancelDelete while cancellation is still available.

args.name: input
args.description: Information required to delete the workspace.

fields.name: organizationDeleteChallenge
fields.description: Requests a deletion confirmation code for the workspace. The code is sent to the requesting user's email and must be used with the organizationDelete mutation to confirm deletion.

fields.name: organizationDomainDelete
fields.description: Removes a domain configuration from the workspace and its authentication settings. Requires workspace-settings permission. Other domain configurations for the workspace are unchanged.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the domain to delete.

fields.name: organizationInviteCreate
fields.description: Invites an email address to the workspace and sends an invitation email. Your role and workspace invitation settings must allow the requested role and teams. Guest invitations require teams; an existing user or unexpired invitation for the address causes an error.

args.name: input
args.description: The organization invite object to create.

fields.name: organizationInviteDelete
fields.description: Deletes (archives) a workspace invite, preventing it from being accepted.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the organization invite to delete.

fields.name: organizationInviteUpdate
fields.description: Replaces the teams an invitee will join on acceptance. Requires permission to manage invitations, and the selected teams must be valid for the invite’s role. This does not change the invitee’s email or role.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the organization invite to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The updates to make to the organization invite object.

fields.name: organizationStartTrial
fields.description: [DEPRECATED] Starts a trial for the workspace.

fields.name: organizationStartTrialForPlan
fields.description: Starts a trial for the workspace on the specified plan type. The workspace must not already be on a paid plan or in an active trial.

args.name: input
args.description: Plan details for trial

fields.name: organizationUpdate
fields.description: Updates the workspace associated with your credentials. Omitted fields keep their current values. Most changes require workspace-settings permission; project and initiative reminder schedules require schedule-management permission. Some settings also depend on the workspace’s plan.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial workspace object to update the workspace with.

fields.name: projectAddLabel
fields.description: Adds a project label while keeping the project’s other labels. The label must be available to the project; label-group and team-scoping rules still apply.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project to add the label to.

args.name: labelId
args.description: The identifier of the label to add.

fields.name: projectArchive
fields.description: Archives a project.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project to archive. Also the identifier from the URL is accepted.

args.name: trash
args.description: Whether to trash the project.

fields.name: projectCreate
fields.description: Creates a project in the supplied teams. You can apply a project template to fill in defaults and create its milestones, initial issues, and initiative associations. The new project must have at least one accessible team.

args.name: aiConversationId
args.description: [Internal] The identifier of the project draft conversation to attach to this project.

args.name: input
args.description: The project properties to set on the new project.

args.name: projectDraftId
args.description: [Internal] The identifier of the project draft that produced this project.

args.name: slackChannelName
args.description: The full name for the Slack channel to create (including prefix). When provided, a Slack channel will be created and connected to the project.

fields.name: projectDelete
fields.description: Moves a project to the trash. This archives the project rather than immediately deleting it permanently. You can restore it with projectUnarchive while it remains available in the trash.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project to delete.

fields.name: projectExternalSyncDisable
fields.description: Disables external sync on a project.

args.name: projectId
args.description: The ID of the project to disable external sync for.

args.name: syncSource
args.description: The source of the external sync to disable.

fields.name: projectLabelCreate
fields.description: Creates a label or label group for projects. Workspace labels require workspace label-management permission; team labels require label-management permission in that team and a plan that supports team project labels. replaceTeamLabels can migrate matching labels into the new scope.

args.name: input
args.description: The project label to create.

args.name: replaceTeamLabels
args.description: Whether to replace all team-specific labels with the same name with this newly created workspace label (default: false).

fields.name: projectLabelDelete
fields.description: Deletes a project label, its children, and inherited copies, removing their assignments from projects.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to delete.

fields.name: projectLabelRestore
fields.description: Restores a previously retired project label, making it available for use on new projects.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to restore.

fields.name: projectLabelRetire
fields.description: Retires a project label. Retired labels remain on existing projects but cannot be applied to new ones.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to retire.

fields.name: projectLabelUpdate
fields.description: Updates the supplied project-label fields and propagates changes to inherited copies. Requires label-management permission for the label’s workspace or team. Update the source label rather than an inherited copy.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the label to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial label object to update.

args.name: replaceTeamLabels
args.description: Whether to replace all team-specific labels with the same name with this updated workspace label (default: false).

fields.name: projectMilestoneCreate
fields.description: Creates a milestone in a project you can edit. Its name must be unique among the project’s active milestones. A milestone starts without issues; assign issues to it separately.

args.name: input
args.description: The project milestone to create.

fields.name: projectMilestoneDelete
fields.description: Permanently deletes a milestone from a project you can edit. The issues are kept in the project, but their milestone association is removed.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project milestone to delete.

fields.name: projectMilestoneUpdate
fields.description: Updates a milestone in a project you can edit, including an archived milestone. Omitted fields keep their current values. Changing projectId moves the milestone and clears its links from issue drafts in the previous project.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project milestone to update. Also the identifier from the URL is accepted.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial object to update the project milestone with.

fields.name: projectRelationCreate
fields.description: Creates a dependency between two different projects using date or milestone anchors.

args.name: input
args.description: The project relation to create.

fields.name: projectRelationDelete
fields.description: Deletes the dependency without deleting either project or milestone.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project relation to delete.

fields.name: projectRelationUpdate
fields.description: Updates the supplied dependency fields and validates both project endpoints.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project relation to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the project relation to update.

fields.name: projectRemoveLabel
fields.description: Removes a project label while keeping the project’s other labels. The label itself is not deleted.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project to remove the label from.

args.name: labelId
args.description: The identifier of the label to remove.

fields.name: projectStatusArchive
fields.description: Archives a project status. The status must not have any active projects assigned to it and must not be the last status of its type.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project status to archive.

fields.name: projectStatusCreate
fields.description: Creates a new project status.

args.name: input
args.description: The ProjectStatus object to create.

fields.name: projectStatusUnarchive
fields.description: Unarchives a project status.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project status to unarchive.

fields.name: projectStatusUpdate
fields.description: Updates a project status.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project status to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial ProjectStatus object to update the ProjectStatus with.

fields.name: projectUnarchive
fields.description: Restores an archived or trashed project. The operation checks the project quota of each associated team before restoring it.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project to restore. Also the identifier from the URL is accepted.

fields.name: projectUpdate
fields.description: Updates the supplied fields of a project you can edit. Omitted fields keep their current values. List inputs such as memberIds and labelIds replace the corresponding lists; see each input for clearing rules and team-access behavior.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project to update. Also the identifier from the URL is accepted.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial project object to update the project with.

fields.name: projectUpdateArchive
fields.description: Archives an update and recalculates the project’s health from the remaining updates. You must be the author or have permission to manage workspace entities. Use projectUpdateUnarchive to restore it.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project update to archive.

fields.name: projectUpdateCreate
fields.description: Publishes a status update for a project you can edit. The update records the current user as author, captures project progress, and refreshes the project’s health. Provide the message in input.body.

args.name: input
args.description: Data for the project update to create.

fields.name: projectUpdateDelete
fields.description: Archives a project update and recalculates project health. Use projectUpdateUnarchive to restore it.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project update to delete.

fields.name: projectUpdateUnarchive
fields.description: Restores an archived update and recalculates the project’s health. The update must currently be archived, and you must be its author or have permission to manage workspace entities.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project update to unarchive.

fields.name: projectUpdateUpdate
fields.description: Edits an update’s message or health. You must be its author or have permission to manage workspace entities. Editing the latest update while it is less than one hour old also refreshes its progress snapshot.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the project update to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the project update to update.

fields.name: pushSubscriptionCreate
fields.description: Registers a browser or device to receive push notifications for the authenticated user. If the same subscription data is already registered, returns that record; otherwise replaces the subscription associated with the current sign-in session. userId in the input is ignored. Successful registration does not guarantee notification delivery; use pushSubscriptionTest to request a test notification.

args.name: input
args.description: The push subscription to create.

fields.name: pushSubscriptionDelete
fields.description: Deletes a push subscription to stop sending notifications through it. Select success to confirm deletion. This operation does not populate entity, so selecting that field produces a GraphQL error.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the push subscription to delete.

fields.name: reactionCreate
fields.description: Adds an emoji reaction as you to one issue, comment, or update. If you already used that emoji on the same resource, the existing reaction is returned. You must be allowed to comment on the target.

args.name: input
args.description: The reaction object to create.

fields.name: reactionDelete
fields.description: Removes a reaction by its UUID and updates the target’s reaction summary. You must be its creator or have workspace permission to manage entities, and you must be allowed to comment on the target.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the reaction to delete.

fields.name: refreshGoogleSheetsData
fields.description: Queues a Google Sheets export refresh. Success confirms scheduling; the returned integration may still contain the previous export state.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the Google Sheets integration to update.

args.name: type
args.description: Export type: issue, project, or initiative. Defaults to issue.

fields.name: releaseArchive
fields.description: Archives a release.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release to archive.

fields.name: releaseComplete
fields.description: Completes the release identified by pipeline and version, or the latest started release when version is omitted. Completing a scheduled release may move its open issues to the next release, according to the pipeline’s rollover setting.

args.name: input
args.description: The input containing the pipeline ID and optional version.

fields.name: releaseCompleteByAccessKey
fields.description: Marks a release as completed using an access key. If version is provided, completes that specific release; otherwise completes the most recent started release. The pipeline is inferred from the access key.

args.name: input
args.description: The input containing the optional version.

fields.name: releaseCreate
fields.description: Creates a new release in a pipeline. If no stage is specified, defaults to the first completed stage for continuous pipelines or the first started stage for scheduled pipelines.

args.name: input
args.description: The release to create.

fields.name: releaseDelete
fields.description: Moves a release to trash for permanent deletion after the retention period. Use releaseUnarchive to restore it before deletion.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release to delete.

fields.name: releaseNoteCreate
fields.description: Creates a note covering releases from one pipeline. Supply explicit release IDs or an inclusive range, plus an optional title and Markdown body. A scheduled pipeline’s note must cover exactly one release.

args.name: input
args.description: The release note fields.

fields.name: releaseNoteDelete
fields.description: Permanently deletes a release note and its body. The covered releases remain.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release note to delete.

fields.name: releaseNoteUpdate
fields.description: Updates a release note’s title, body, or covered releases. Omitted fields remain unchanged, and a new release selection replaces the old one. The note stays in its original pipeline.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release note to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The fields to update.

fields.name: releasePipelineArchive
fields.description: Archives a pipeline and schedules archival of its releases. The release changes run in the background, so they may not be complete when this mutation returns. Requires workspace team-management permission or ownership of every associated team.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release pipeline to archive.

fields.name: releasePipelineCreate
fields.description: Creates a release pipeline with default stages, subject to your workspace’s plan and quota. Requires workspace team-management permission or ownership of every team associated with the pipeline.

args.name: input
args.description: The ReleasePipeline object to create.

fields.name: releasePipelineDelete
fields.description: Moves a pipeline and its releases to the trash for permanent deletion after the retention period. Repeating the operation does not extend that period. Requires workspace team-management permission or ownership of every associated team.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release pipeline to delete.

fields.name: releasePipelineUnarchive
fields.description: Restores a pipeline and schedules restoration of its archived releases. Individually trashed releases are left in the trash. The release changes run in the background, and the same pipeline administration permissions apply.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release pipeline to unarchive.

fields.name: releasePipelineUpdate
fields.description: Updates an existing release pipeline. Supports updating name, slug, type, production flag, path patterns, and team associations. Private teams that the current user cannot access are preserved in the team list.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release pipeline to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial ReleasePipeline object to update the ReleasePipeline with.

fields.name: releaseStageArchive
fields.description: Archives a release stage. Only started-type stages can be archived, and only if they have no active releases and at least one other stage of the same type remains. Cannot archive the last non-frozen started stage.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release stage to archive.

fields.name: releaseStageCreate
fields.description: Creates a new release stage in a pipeline. Non-started stages must use default names and colors and are unique by type; creating a canonical duplicate returns the existing stage. Started stages can optionally be frozen, but at least one non-frozen started stage must remain.

args.name: input
args.description: The ReleaseStage object to create.

fields.name: releaseStageUnarchive
fields.description: Unarchives a release stage.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release stage to unarchive.

fields.name: releaseStageUpdate
fields.description: Updates an existing release stage. Only started-type stages can be edited. Supports updating name, color, position, and frozen status.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release stage to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial ReleaseStage object to update the ReleaseStage with.

fields.name: releaseSync
fields.description: Associates issues found in issue or pull request references with a release. Continuous pipelines create completed releases and reuse an existing version only when its commit SHA matches. Scheduled pipelines accumulate issues in an open release or use the supplied version. Existing issue associations are kept unless explicitly reverted in a scheduled pipeline.

args.name: input
args.description: The release data to sync.

fields.name: releaseSyncByAccessKey
fields.description: Syncs release data using an access key for CI/CD integration. The pipeline is automatically inferred from the access key's configured resources, so no pipeline ID is needed in the input.

args.name: input
