args.description: The release data to sync.

fields.name: releaseUnarchive
fields.description: Restores an archived or trashed release before it is permanently deleted. The release keeps its pipeline and saved issue associations.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release to unarchive.

fields.name: releaseUpdate
fields.description: Updates a release by ID. Omitted fields remain unchanged. A release cannot move to another pipeline.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the release to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial Release object to update the Release with.

fields.name: releaseUpdateByPipeline
fields.description: Updates a release by pipeline identifier. Finds the release by version, otherwise the latest started release or else the planned release with the earliest target date, and optionally transitions it to a new stage by name.

args.name: input
args.description: The input containing the pipeline ID, optional version, and optional stage name.

fields.name: releaseUpdateByPipelineByAccessKey
fields.description: Updates a release by pipeline using an access key.

args.name: input
args.description: The input containing the optional version and optional stage name.

fields.name: resendOrganizationInvite
fields.description: Re-sends a workspace invitation email for the specified invite ID.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the organization invite to re-send.

fields.name: resendOrganizationInviteByEmail
fields.description: Re-sends a workspace invitation email to the specified email address, if an outstanding invite exists for that address.

fields.name: samlTokenUserAccountAuth
fields.description: Completes SAML sign-in with the email and token issued by the SAML flow, then sets the authentication cookie. The response identifies workspace memberships and any workspaces that require a different sign-in method. Unlike email token sign-in, this operation does not require clientAuthCode.

args.name: input
args.description: The data used for token authentication.

fields.name: teamCreate
fields.description: Creates a team with workflow states, labels, and other initial resources. You become a member and, for private teams or plans that support team owners, an owner. copySettingsFromTeamId copies settings and related resources from an existing team; copied settings take precedence over input values except an explicit private value.

args.name: copySettingsFromTeamId
args.description: The team id to copy settings from, if any.

args.name: input
args.description: The team object to create.

fields.name: teamCyclesDelete
fields.description: Permanently deletes all cycles for a team and disables cycles. Issues are kept, but their cycle associations are removed. Requires permission to manage the team.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the team, which cycles will be deleted.

fields.name: teamDelete
fields.description: Archives a team and schedules permanent deletion after a 30-day grace period. You cannot delete the workspace’s final active team. Requires a workspace administrator or team owner; use teamUnarchive before deletion begins to restore it.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the team to delete.

fields.name: teamKeyDelete
fields.description: Deletes a previously used team key. The active team key (the team's current key) cannot be deleted.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the team key to delete.

fields.name: teamMembershipCreate
fields.description: Adds a user to an active team after checking permission and membership limits. Regular workspace members also join ancestor teams. The operation fails if the user is already a member or if the team is archived, retired, or managed through SCIM.

args.name: input
args.description: The team membership object to create.

fields.name: teamMembershipDelete
fields.description: Removes a user from a team after checking removal permissions and membership restrictions. Leaving cannot remove the user’s last active team, and SCIM-managed memberships must be managed through the identity provider. alsoLeaveParentTeams can extend the removal to parent teams.

args.name: alsoLeaveParentTeams
args.description: Whether to leave the parent teams.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the team membership to delete.

fields.name: teamMembershipUpdate
fields.description: Updates the team’s position in the member’s team list.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the team membership to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial team membership object to update the team membership with.

fields.name: teamUnarchive
fields.description: Restores an archived team and cancels its scheduled deletion while the grace period still permits cancellation. Requires workspace team-management permission, access to the team, and capacity for another active team on the workspace’s plan.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the team to unarchive.

fields.name: teamUpdate
fields.description: Updates the supplied team fields. Changes require the relevant team-management permissions.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the team to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial team object to update the team with.

args.name: mapping
args.description: [INTERNAL] Mapping of existing team entities to those inherited from the parent team

fields.name: templateCreate
fields.description: Create a template. Requires permission to manage templates in the workspace, team, or release pipeline that owns it.

args.name: input
args.description: The template object to create.

fields.name: templateDelete
fields.description: Deletes a template and its inherited copies. Requires permission to manage templates in its scope; inherited copies must be deleted at their source. Resources already created from the template remain.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the template to delete.

fields.name: templateUpdate
fields.description: Changes a template’s metadata, saved defaults, or team scope. Update an inherited template at its source, and supply the full templateData when replacing its configuration. Changing a template does not rewrite resources already created from it.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the template.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the template to update.

fields.name: timeScheduleCreate
fields.description: Creates an API-managed on-call schedule in the workspace. Provide a name and the complete list of shifts, then reference the returned schedule ID from a triage responsibility to use it for a team. An OAuth-created schedule is owned by that application for later updates and deletion. Duplicate IDs or external IDs are rejected.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the time schedule to create.

fields.name: timeScheduleDelete
fields.description: Deletes an API-managed schedule and replaces linked triage responsibilities with available fallback users. The same ownership and team-management requirements as timeScheduleUpdate apply. Integration-synced schedules cannot be deleted here.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the time schedule to delete.

fields.name: timeScheduleRefreshIntegrationSchedule
fields.description: Requests a refresh of a schedule managed by an integration. The schedule must have an associated integration. Success means the refresh was queued; the returned timeSchedule may still contain its previous shifts. Query the schedule again to read the refreshed entries.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the time schedule to refresh.

fields.name: timeScheduleUpdate
fields.description: Updates an unarchived, API-managed schedule. Omitted fields remain unchanged; entries replaces every existing shift. OAuth callers can update only schedules created by the same application. Other callers need management permission for every team using the schedule, or workspace team management permission if no team uses it. Integration-synced schedules cannot be edited here.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the time schedule to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the time schedule to update.

fields.name: timeScheduleUpsertExternal
fields.description: Finds an unarchived schedule by its workspace-unique externalId and updates it, or creates one if none exists. For a new schedule, include name and the same externalId inside input; the lookup argument is not copied into input automatically. A supplied entries list replaces the old shifts. Email references without userId are matched to workspace users when possible; unmatched references remain external. The same ownership rules as timeScheduleUpdate apply to an existing schedule.

args.name: externalId
args.description: Schedule identifier in the external service, unique within the workspace.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the time schedule to insert or update.

fields.name: trackAnonymousEvent
fields.description: Submits an anonymous $pageview or $pageleave analytics event, with optional properties and session correlation. Unsupported event names return success=false. A successful response means tracking accepted the event, not that analytics delivery has completed. Limited to 30 requests per hour.

args.name: input
args.description: Event tracking details.

fields.name: triageResponsibilityCreate
fields.description: Creates the team’s triage responsibility using a manual user selection or an on-call schedule. The team must be writable, the workspace plan must support triage responsibility, and the caller needs team management permission. A team can have only one rule. Selecting an integration-managed schedule also queues a refresh of its shifts.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the triage responsibility to create.

fields.name: triageResponsibilityDelete
fields.description: Deletes a triage responsibility.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the triage responsibility to delete.

fields.name: triageResponsibilityUpdate
fields.description: Updates the action or responsible users for a writable team’s existing rule. Changing to a manual selection clears its schedule, and changing to a schedule clears its manual selection. Omitted fields remain unchanged. Requires team management permission; selecting a different integration-managed schedule queues a refresh.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the triage responsibility to update.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the triage responsibility to update.

fields.name: userChangeRole
fields.description: Changes the workspace role of a user. The requesting user must have a role equal to or higher than the target role. Requires workspace admin permissions.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the user

args.name: role
args.description: The new role for the user.

fields.name: userDiscordConnect
fields.description: Connects the Discord user to this Linear account via OAuth2.

args.name: code
args.description: The Discord OAuth code.

args.name: redirectUri
args.description: The Discord OAuth redirect URI.

fields.name: userExternalUserDisconnect
fields.description: Disconnects the external user from this Linear account.

args.name: service
args.description: The external service to disconnect.

args.name: workspaceIntegrationId
args.description: The workspace Jira integration whose account mapping to remove. If omitted, removes all Jira mappings without a personal connection.

fields.name: userFlagUpdate
fields.description: Updates a specific user settings flag by performing an operation (e.g., increment or clear) on it.

args.name: flag
args.description: Settings flag to increment.

args.name: operation
args.description: Flag operation to perform.

fields.name: userRevokeAllSessions
fields.description: Revokes all active sessions for a user, forcing them to re-authenticate. Can only be called by a workspace admin or owner.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the user to logout all sessions of.

fields.name: userRevokeSession
fields.description: Revokes a specific authentication session for a user. The admin cannot revoke their own sessions with this mutation. Can only be called by a workspace admin or owner.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the user whose session to revoke.

args.name: sessionId
args.description: The identifier of the session to revoke.

fields.name: userSettingsFlagsReset
fields.description: Resets one or more of the user's setting flags. If no specific flags are provided, all flags are reset.

args.name: flags
args.description: The flags to reset. If not provided all flags will be reset.

fields.name: userSettingsUpdate
fields.description: Updates the settings record identified by id. You must own that record or have permission to manage workspace entities. General settings and notification category or channel preferences merge with existing values. See notificationDeliveryPreferences for its schedule replacement and mobile-channel effects.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the userSettings to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial notification object to update the settings with.

fields.name: userSuspend
fields.description: Suspends a user, deactivating their account and revoking access to the workspace. The suspended user's sessions are invalidated. Can only be called by a workspace admin or owner.

args.name: forceBypassScimRestrictions
args.description: [INTERNAL] Whether to bypass SCIM restrictions when suspending. Use with caution — this overrides identity provider management.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the user to suspend.

fields.name: userUnlinkFromIdentityProvider
fields.description: Unlinks a guest user from their identity provider. Can only be called by an admin when SCIM is enabled.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the guest user to unlink from their identity provider.

fields.name: userUnsuspend
fields.description: Re-activates a suspended user, restoring their access to the workspace. Can only be called by a workspace admin or owner.

args.name: forceBypassScimRestrictions
args.description: [INTERNAL] Whether to bypass SCIM restrictions when unsuspending. Use with caution — this overrides identity provider management.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the user to unsuspend.

fields.name: userUpdate
fields.description: Updates a user’s profile. Use the user UUID or me for your own account. Updating another user requires member-management permission; identity-provider rules may block name changes, and application accounts only accept name and displayName.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the user to update. Use `me` to reference currently authenticated user.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial user object to update the user with.

fields.name: viewPreferencesCreate
fields.description: Saves display settings for a view and scope. Existing records that conflict with the supplied type, view type, and scope are deleted and replaced, so supply the settings you want to retain. Personal preferences are owned by the current user.

args.name: input
args.description: The ViewPreferences object to create.

fields.name: viewPreferencesDelete
fields.description: Deletes a saved preferences record, allowing the view to use its fallback defaults. You can delete only your own user-type preferences. If the record is already absent, the mutation still succeeds.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the ViewPreferences to delete.

fields.name: viewPreferencesUpdate
fields.description: Replaces the supplied settings objects on a saved preferences record. You can update only your own user-type preferences; changing workspace defaults for a custom view also requires permission to edit that view.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the ViewPreferences object.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the view preferences.

fields.name: webhookCreate
fields.description: Creates a webhook subscription and returns its configuration, including the signing secret. Choose one team or all public teams, and provide a public HTTPS destination with the resource types you want to receive. The destination must not already be registered for the same team scope. Requires workspace API management permission; a team-specific webhook also requires that team’s management permission. AuditEntry subscriptions have separate audit log access requirements.

args.name: input
args.description: The webhook object to create.

fields.name: webhookDelete
fields.description: Deletes a webhook subscription and stops future deliveries.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the Webhook to delete.

fields.name: webhookRotateSecret
fields.description: Generates and returns a new HMAC-SHA256 signing secret for the webhook. Update your receiver to verify later deliveries with the returned key; the previous key is replaced rather than kept as a second active key. This changes webhook signatures, not the endpoint or subscribed event streams.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the Webhook to rotate the secret for.

fields.name: webhookUpdate
fields.description: Updates an existing webhook without changing its team scope. Omitted properties remain unchanged, and resourceTypes replaces the complete list of event streams. Setting enabled to false pauses delivery while retaining the subscription. Changing secret changes the key your receiver must use for later deliveries. Requires workspace API management permission and access to the subscribed resource types.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the Webhook.

args.name: input
args.description: The properties of the Webhook.

fields.name: workflowStateArchive
fields.description: Archives an unused status so it is no longer available for new issues. First move or archive every active issue in that status. You must be able to manage the team, and cannot archive reserved or inherited statuses or the last active status of a type.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the state to archive.

fields.name: workflowStateCreate
fields.description: Add an issue status to a team. Requires permission to manage the team; inherited workflows cannot be edited directly.

args.name: input
args.description: The state to create.

fields.name: workflowStateUpdate
fields.description: Update a status’s name, color, description, or position. Requires permission to manage the team. Reserved and inherited statuses cannot be changed.

args.name: id
args.description: The identifier of the state to update.

args.name: input
args.description: A partial state object to update.

types.name: Notification
types.description: An activity notification sent to a workspace member. Its concrete type identifies the related entity, while type identifies the event that occurred. Read, snooze, and archive states belong to the recipient. The inbox can group several related notifications into one item.

fields.name: actor
fields.description: The user that caused the notification. Null if the notification was triggered by a non-user actor such as an integration, external user, or system event.

fields.name: archivedAt
fields.description: When the resource was archived, in UTC. Null while active, including after unarchiving. Archived resources still exist but are normally excluded from lists unless `includeArchived` is true.

fields.name: botActor
fields.description: The bot that caused the notification.

fields.name: category
fields.description: The category of the notification.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: The resource’s recorded creation time, in UTC. Imports may preserve an earlier creation time.

fields.name: emailedAt
fields.description: The time at which an email reminder for this notification was sent to the user. Null if no email reminder has been sent.

fields.name: externalUserActor
fields.description: The external user that caused the notification. Populated when the notification was triggered by an external user (e.g., a commenter from a connected integration like Slack or GitHub) rather than a Linear workspace member.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The resource's unique UUID. This stays unchanged when the resource is renamed or moved; use it for stored references and mutations.

fields.name: readAt
fields.description: The time at which the user marked the notification as read. Null if the notification is unread.

fields.name: snoozedUntilAt
fields.description: The time until which a notification is snoozed. After this time, the notification reappears in the user's inbox. Null if the notification is not currently snoozed.

fields.name: type
fields.description: Notification type. Determines the kind of event that triggered this notification and which associated entity fields will be populated.

fields.name: unsnoozedAt
fields.description: The time at which a notification was unsnoozed. Null if the notification has not been unsnoozed.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the resource was last meaningfully updated, in UTC. Some background or housekeeping changes do not advance this timestamp.

fields.name: user
fields.description: The recipient user of this notification.

types.name: NotificationArchivePayload

fields.name: entity

fields.name: lastSyncId
fields.description: Synchronization cursor used by Linear clients. External integrations can ignore this field.

fields.name: success
fields.description: Whether the operation was successful.

fields.name: notifications

fields.name: success
fields.description: Whether the operation was successful.

types.name: NotificationCategory

types.name: NotificationCategoryPreferences

fields.name: appsAndIntegrations

fields.name: assignments

fields.name: billing
fields.description: The preferences for billing notifications.

fields.name: commentsAndReplies
fields.description: The preferences for notifications about comments and replies.

fields.name: customers
fields.description: The preferences for customer notifications.

fields.name: documentChanges
fields.description: The preferences for notifications about document changes.

fields.name: feed

fields.name: loops
fields.description: The preferences for notifications about loops.

fields.name: mentions

fields.name: postsAndUpdates
fields.description: The preferences for notifications about posts and updates.

inputFields.description: Conditions on the initiative update being discussed. Use null: false to select comments on initiative updates.

inputFields.name: issue
inputFields.description: Conditions on the issue directly associated with the comment. Use documentContent to filter comments attached to an issue’s description content instead.

inputFields.name: needs
inputFields.description: Conditions on customer requests linked to the comment. Use some to require a matching request or length to count linked requests.

inputFields.name: null
inputFields.description: Use true to match an unset comment relation, or false to require it to be set. Omit this field when you only want to test the related record’s properties.

inputFields.name: or
inputFields.description: Alternative conditions; the comment must match at least one. Other fields at this level must still match. An empty list adds no condition.

inputFields.name: parent
inputFields.description: Conditions on the thread’s root comment. Use null: true to return root comments, or null: false to return replies. An ID condition selects replies in one thread.

inputFields.name: project
inputFields.description: Filters that the comment's project must satisfy.

inputFields.name: projectUpdate
inputFields.description: Conditions on the project update being discussed. Use null: false to select comments on project updates.

inputFields.name: reactions
inputFields.description: Conditions on the comment’s emoji reactions. Use some with an emoji condition to find comments that received that reaction, or length to test the total reaction count.

inputFields.name: updatedAt
inputFields.description: Filters by the last meaningful update time. Some background changes do not advance it. Use `gte` and `lt` together to select a time window.

inputFields.name: user
inputFields.description: Conditions on the user recorded as the comment’s author. This does not match an app’s separate display attribution.

inputFields.description: Whether the current time falls within the cycle’s start and end times. Use team to restrict the result to one team’s schedule.

inputFields.description: Whether the cycle has completed and its next numbered cycle has not started yet. This identifies the completed cycle during the team’s gap between cycles.

inputFields.name: isPast
inputFields.description: Whether the cycle’s end time has passed. This is independent of whether its completion step has run.

Combine `gte` and `lt` for a time window. Use `{ null: true }` for missing timestamps; `nin` also includes missing values, while `neq` and range comparisons do not.

inputFields.name: neq

inputFields.name: nin

inputFields.name: null

inputFields.description: Conditions on when the issue was automatically closed after inactivity. The value is cleared when its status changes.

inputFields.name: canceledAt
inputFields.description: Conditions on when the issue entered a canceled or duplicate status. The value is cleared when the issue leaves those status types.

inputFields.description: Conditions on the number of distinct customers with active, important requests linked to the issue. Important requests without a customer record each count separately. Supply one comparison; to apply a range, put separate customerImportantCount conditions in and.

inputFields.description: Whether another issue blocks this issue, with both issues still open. A link with a closed issue counts under hasRelatedRelations instead.

inputFields.name: hasBlockingRelations

inputFields.name: hasDismissedAgentSessions

inputFields.name: hasDuplicateRelations

inputFields.name: hasErroredAgentSessions
inputFields.description: Comparator for filtering issues bucketed as having an errored agent session, no active sessions, and no merged agent pull requests.

inputFields.name: hasMergedAgentPullRequests
inputFields.description: Comparator for filtering issues which have agent-session-linked pull requests that were merged.

inputFields.name: hasRelatedRelations
inputFields.description: Whether the issue has a related link in either direction. Blocking links also count as related when either issue is closed; open blocking relationships are covered by hasBlockingRelations and hasBlockedByRelations.

inputFields.name: hasSuggestedAssignees

inputFields.name: and
inputFields.description: All of these nested filters must match, in addition to the other conditions on this filter.

inputFields.name: createdAt
inputFields.description: Filters by creation time. Use a fixed timestamp or a relative duration, such as `{ gte: "-P7D" }` for resources created in the last seven days.

inputFields.name: id
inputFields.description: Filters by the resource's stable UUID. Use `eq` for one ID or `in` for a list of IDs.

inputFields.name: or
inputFields.description: At least one of these nested filters must match, in addition to the other conditions on this filter. An empty list is ignored.

inputFields.name: project
inputFields.description: Filters that the project update project must satisfy.

inputFields.name: reactions
inputFields.description: Filters that the project updates reactions must satisfy.

inputFields.name: updatedAt
inputFields.description: Filters by the last meaningful update time. Some background changes do not advance it. Use `gte` and `lt` together to select a time window.

inputFields.name: user
inputFields.description: Filters that the project update creator must satisfy.

types.name: ProjectUpdateInput
types.description: Changes to a project. Omit a field to keep its current value. Lists replace the corresponding selections unless their description says otherwise; null only clears fields that explicitly support it.

inputFields.name: canceledAt
inputFields.description: The time at which the project was canceled.

inputFields.name: color
inputFields.description: The color of the project.

inputFields.name: completedAt
inputFields.description: The time at which the project was completed.

inputFields.name: content
inputFields.description: Replacement project overview in Markdown. Empty strings, null, and omission leave the existing content unchanged.

inputFields.name: convertedFromIssueId
inputFields.description: The ID of the issue from which that project is created.

inputFields.name: description
inputFields.description: A short plain-text summary. Use an empty string to clear it; null is not accepted.

inputFields.name: frequencyResolution
inputFields.description: The unit of updateReminderFrequency: daily or weekly.

inputFields.name: icon
inputFields.description: The icon of the project.

inputFields.name: labelIds
inputFields.description: The replacement list of project label UUIDs. Use [] to remove all labels, or omit the field to keep them. Use projectAddLabel or projectRemoveLabel when you only need to change one label; team and label-group rules apply to both approaches.

inputFields.name: lastAppliedTemplateId
inputFields.description: Records the last applied template UUID without applying its contents.

inputFields.name: leadId
inputFields.description: UUID of the project lead. Pass null to remove the lead. Application users cannot be leads; a new lead is added as a member.

inputFields.name: memberIds
inputFields.description: The replacement list of project member UUIDs. Use [] to remove all members except the project lead, who remains a member. Application users cannot be added; omit the field to keep the current members.

inputFields.name: name
inputFields.description: The name of the project.

inputFields.name: priority
inputFields.description: The priority of the project. 0 = No priority, 1 = Urgent, 2 = High, 3 = Medium, 4 = Low.

inputFields.name: prioritySortOrder
inputFields.description: The sort order for the project within shared views, when ordered by priority.

inputFields.name: projectUpdateRemindersPausedUntilAt
inputFields.description: The time until which project update reminders are paused. Set null to remove the project-specific pause; reminders still follow the configured schedule. Omit to leave the pause unchanged.

inputFields.name: slackIssueComments
inputFields.description: Whether to send new issue comment notifications to Slack.

inputFields.name: slackIssueStatuses
inputFields.description: Whether to send issue status update notifications to Slack.

inputFields.name: slackNewIssue
inputFields.description: Whether to send new issue notifications to Slack.

inputFields.name: sortOrder
inputFields.description: Position in shared project views, in ascending order. Pass 0 to append; collisions are adjusted.

inputFields.name: startDate
inputFields.description: The planned start date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Null clears the date.

inputFields.name: startDateResolution
inputFields.description: The precision of startDate: month, quarter, halfYear, or year. Null uses an exact date.

inputFields.name: statusId
inputFields.description: The UUID of an active project status available to the project’s lead team. Moving between status types updates startedAt, completedAt, or canceledAt as appropriate. Omit to keep the current status.

inputFields.name: targetDate
inputFields.description: The planned completion date in YYYY-MM-DD format. Null clears the date.

inputFields.name: targetDateResolution
inputFields.description: The precision of targetDate: month, quarter, halfYear, or year. Null uses an exact date.

inputFields.name: teamIds
inputFields.description: The replacement list of team UUIDs. Teams you cannot access are preserved, so omitting a private team does not remove it. At least one team must remain, and a team with active project issues cannot be removed until those issues are moved.

inputFields.name: trashed
inputFields.description: The stored trash flag. This field does not archive or restore the project. Use projectDelete to move it to the trash and projectUnarchive to restore it.

inputFields.name: updateReminderFrequency
inputFields.description: The interval between update reminders, in the unit given by frequencyResolution. Null inherits the workspace setting; omit to leave unchanged.

inputFields.name: updateReminderFrequencyInWeeks
inputFields.description: The interval between update reminders in weeks. Null inherits the workspace setting; omit to leave unchanged.

inputFields.name: updateRemindersDay
inputFields.description: The day of the week on which to prompt for project updates.

inputFields.name: updateRemindersHour
inputFields.description: The hour of the day (0-23) at which to prompt for project updates.

types.name: PullRequestComment
types.description: A comment on a pull request, synced bidirectionally with the hosting provider (e.g., GitHub). Comments can be top-level or threaded replies, and may be associated with specific code locations via an anchor. Comments belonging to a pending review are not visible to other users or synced to the provider until the review is submitted.

fields.name: archivedAt
fields.description: When the resource was archived, in UTC. Null while active, including after unarchiving. Archived resources still exist but are normally excluded from lists unless `includeArchived` is true.

fields.name: bodyData
fields.description: The comment content as a ProseMirror document.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: The resource’s recorded creation time, in UTC. Imports may preserve an earlier creation time.

fields.name: decision
fields.description: The review decision this comment was submitted with (approved, changes requested, commented, or dismissed). Set on the summary comment of a submitted review. Null for all other comments.

fields.name: editedAt
fields.description: The time at which the comment was edited. Null if never edited.

fields.name: externalReviewId
fields.description: Provider-specific identifier of the review this comment was submitted with (e.g., the GitHub review ID). All comments from one review submission share the same value. Null if the comment was not part of a provider review, or the identifier has not synced from the provider yet.

fields.name: externalThreadId
fields.description: Provider-specific thread identifier. Null if the provider did not provide a thread identifier.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The resource's unique UUID. This stays unchanged when the resource is renamed or moved; use it for stored references and mutations.

fields.name: pendingReviewId
fields.description: Identifier of the review this comment was created in when composed in Linear. Comments submitted together keep the same value after submission. Null if the comment was not created through a review composed in Linear.

fields.name: reactionData
fields.description: Emoji reaction summary for this pull request comment, grouped by emoji type. Each entry contains the emoji name, count, and the IDs of users who reacted.

fields.name: resolvedAt
fields.description: The time at which the top-level thread was resolved. Null if unresolved.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the resource was last meaningfully updated, in UTC. Some background or housekeeping changes do not advance this timestamp.

fields.name: url

types.name: Webhook
types.description: A subscription that delivers Linear events to your HTTPS endpoint as signed HTTP POST requests. resourceTypes selects the event streams, while the team settings limit which team events are included. Manually created webhooks have their own URL and signing secret; OAuth application webhooks use the application’s configuration. Verify payload signatures before processing events, and use enabled to pause delivery without deleting the subscription.

fields.name: allPublicTeams
fields.description: Whether to receive events from all public teams in the workspace, including public teams created later.

fields.name: archivedAt
fields.description: When the resource was archived, in UTC. Null while active, including after unarchiving. Archived resources still exist but are normally excluded from lists unless `includeArchived` is true.

fields.name: createdAt
fields.description: The resource’s recorded creation time, in UTC. Imports may preserve an earlier creation time.

fields.name: creator
fields.description: The user who created the webhook. Null if the creator is unavailable or it was created for an OAuth application.

fields.name: enabled
fields.description: Whether the webhook is enabled. When disabled, no payloads will be delivered even if matching events occur.

fields.name: id
fields.description: The resource's unique UUID. This stays unchanged when the resource is renamed or moved; use it for stored references and mutations.

fields.name: label
fields.description: A human-readable label for the webhook, used for identification in the UI. Null if no label has been set.

fields.name: resourceTypes
fields.description: The resource types this webhook is subscribed to (e.g., 'Issue', 'Comment', 'Project', 'Cycle'). The webhook will only receive payloads for events affecting these resource types.

fields.name: secret
fields.description: The secret used to sign webhook payloads with HMAC-SHA256. Your receiver uses it to verify that a request came from Linear and that the body has not changed. Keep it private and update your receiver when rotating it. Null means the secret is unavailable on this record, as with an OAuth webhook whose signing configuration belongs to the application.

fields.name: team
fields.description: The team whose events this webhook receives. Null when the subscription is not limited to one team.

fields.name: updatedAt
fields.description: When the resource was last meaningfully updated, in UTC. Some background or housekeeping changes do not advance this timestamp.

fields.name: url

types.name: __Directive
types.description:
A Directive provides a way to describe alternate runtime execution and type validation behavior in a GraphQL document.

In some cases, you need to provide options to alter GraphQL's execution behavior in ways field arguments will not suffice, such as conditionally including or skipping a field. Directives provide this by describing additional information to the executor.

types.description: A Directive can be adjacent to many parts of the GraphQL language, a __DirectiveLocation describes one such possible adjacencies.

types.name: __EnumValue
types.description: One possible value for a given Enum. Enum values are unique values, not a placeholder for a string or numeric value. However an Enum value is returned in a JSON response as a string.

types.name: __Field
types.description: Object and Interface types are described by a list of Fields, each of which has a name, potentially a list of arguments, and a return type.

types.name: __InputValue

fields.name: defaultValue

types.name: __Schema
types.description: A GraphQL Schema defines the capabilities of a GraphQL server. It exposes all available types and directives on the server, as well as the entry points for query, mutation, and subscription operations.

fields.name: types
fields.description: A list of all types supported by this server.

fields.name: queryType
fields.description: The type that query operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: mutationType
fields.description: If this server supports mutation, the type that mutation operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: subscriptionType
fields.description: If this server support subscription, the type that subscription operations will be rooted at.

fields.name: directives
fields.description: A list of all directives supported by this server.

types.name: __Type
types.description:
The fundamental unit of any GraphQL Schema is the type. There are many kinds of types in GraphQL as represented by the `__TypeKind` enum.

Depending on the kind of a type, certain fields describe information about that type. Scalar types provide no information beyond a name, description and optional `specifiedByUrl`, while Enum types provide their values. Object and Interface types provide the fields they describe. Abstract types, Union and Interface, provide the Object types possible at runtime. List and NonNull types compose other types.

types.name: __TypeKind
types.description: An enum describing what kind of type a given `__Type` is.

enumValues.name: SCALAR
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a scalar.

enumValues.name: OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an object. `fields` and `interfaces` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: INTERFACE
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an interface. `fields`, `interfaces`, and `possibleTypes` are valid fields.

enumValues.name: UNION
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a union. `possibleTypes` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: ENUM
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an enum. `enumValues` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: INPUT_OBJECT
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is an input object. `inputFields` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: LIST
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a list. `ofType` is a valid field.

enumValues.name: NON_NULL
enumValues.description: Indicates this type is a non-null. `ofType` is a valid field.
